baseline_models.focus_anchor: The recognition clause, `in the faces ... al-munkar`, is enclosed by the two occurrences of reciting the signs.
baseline_models.mechanism: Manifest signs arrive as a followed vocal sequence. The addressees try to cover or refuse recognition, yet the face becomes a second sign whose visible marks disclose that refusal before the almost-assault becomes action.

activation_trace.role: Followed succession supplies the continuous recitation relay enclosing the facial reaction.
A visibly manifest sign supplies the evidence that provokes and diagnoses the response.
Emergence into clarity makes concealment unstable and prepares the counter-disclosure on the face.
Visible facial marks make the face a readable evidentiary surface rather than a neutral location.
Covering supplies the concealed act that the involuntary facial sign exposes.
Nonrecognition and denial create the paradox that their refusal is itself recognizable.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports that hostile disbelievers look angry when scripture is read.
changed_reading.after: The signs generate an involuntary counter-sign: the face makes attempted covering and nonrecognition recognizable before the hand moves.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The double recitation, the almost-assault, the imperative `say`, the announcement, and the promised destination form a sequence of speech and response.
baseline_models.mechanism: Sound follows sound until the hearers nearly answer speech with bodily force. The command to speak converts that imminent force back into an announced warning, and the warning extends the short human almost-action into a divinely fixed outcome.

activation_trace.role: One voice following another supplies the audible relay that bodily force tries to answer.
Nearness to action holds the assault at an unstable threshold rather than reporting a completed blow.
Uttered speech supplies the authorized counter-move to the threatened bodily response.
A consequential report turns the counter-speech into disclosure of an outcome.
Threatening promise gives the announced fire binding forward force.
Arrival at an outcome closes the sequence that their merely imminent action begins.

changed_reading.before: A warning of fire follows an angry interruption.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a contest of media and timing: recited speech elicits almost-violence, then authorized speech encloses that impulse within a promised outcome.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The face presently displays what denial tries to cover, while the promised fire and bad destination occupy the final clause.
baseline_models.mechanism: The fire inventory also carries illumination, branding, and a clear track. That makes the punishment coexist with a disclosure model: the face is the preliminary visible mark of covered refusal, and fire is its irreversible final manifestation.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies what both the face and final fire progressively uncover.
A mark recognizable on the face supplies the present, partial disclosure.
Kindled fire together with fire-branding supplies punishment as an imposed visible mark.
A clear projecting track lets the fire function as final exposure as well as pain.
The committed promise carries the partial present sign toward a future manifestation.
Final becoming turns disclosure from a passing expression into an enduring end-state.

changed_reading.before: The face shows anger now and fire punishes later.
changed_reading.after: Present face and future fire form two degrees of disclosure: refusal first leaks through a readable surface and finally becomes an inescapable manifested condition.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier scene presents a visible syndrome, apparent intoxication, while denying the shallow causal label. This revises facial recognition in the focus: the surface can be evidentially true while its first conventional classification is false, so `you recognize` is an abductive diagnosis of refusal from its bodily trace.

activation_trace.role: Visual and inward seeing supplies the act of reading a bodily appearance as evidence.
Loss-of-sobriety imagery supplies the visible syndrome whose literal label the ayah immediately refuses.
Recognition by an effect or mark supplies the inferential bridge from face to concealed stance.
The outward-facing surface is the site where the inner cause becomes diagnostically available.

structural_cues: 22:2 says people are seen as intoxicated and immediately denies literal intoxication; 22:72 locates recognition in faces.
In the focus ayah, recognition precedes the almost-assault, so diagnosis is registered before action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a mismatch between visible syndrome and naive label; I infer that the focus reader identifies the deeper cause from a facial symptom. A live alternative is that the face simply displays ordinary anger without demanding diagnostic caution.

changed_reading.before: The facial munkar is a transparent emotional expression.
changed_reading.after: The face is a diagnostic surface: its disturbance is real evidence, but recognition must identify the concealed refusal rather than stop at an obvious emotion label.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier worshipper under trial turns over upon his face. That gives the focus face directional force: it is not only an expressive surface but the front on which allegiance reverses, with visible denial approaching a turn from hearing into attack.

activation_trace.role: Turning a thing from its face supplies the reversal that converts pressure into changed orientation.
Direction and destination make the face the leading edge of the worshipper's reversal.
The visible front anchors that directional model in the focus facial clause.
Change into an unrecognized or hated state supplies the altered orientation visible on the face.

structural_cues: 22:11 binds inversion directly to `upon his face` after trial.
22:72 moves from the face to an almost-completed assault, giving the visible turn a possible bodily continuation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies face-bound reversal in 22:11 and face-bound rejection in 22:72; I infer a shared orientation mechanism from reception to turning away and outward attack. A live alternative is that the repeated face language is only idiomatic and the two scenes remain independent.

changed_reading.after: Faces register a vector of allegiance: the refusal has turned the hearer away from reception and nearly forward into violence.

context_deltas.mechanism: A connection is extended, cut, tested as a scheme, and tied to pent rage in 22:15. Against the focus's doubled recitation sequence, this activates the near-assault as an interruption tactic: force aims to sever the human link carrying the signs because the signs themselves cannot be answered.

activation_trace.role: A rope-like connection supplies a material analogue for the reciter-to-hearer link.
Severance supplies the directional action assigned to threatened force against the relay.
Machination supplies purposeful interference rather than a purely reflexive outburst.
Anguish held in the chest supplies the pressure that seeks release through interruption.
Followed succession makes the repeated recitation a relay capable of being interrupted.
The split machination branch lets the context sharpen the near-action as possible strategy without replacing its ordinary threshold sense.

structural_cues: 22:15 orders connection, cutting, inspection, scheme, and rage in one chain.
22:72 repeats the recitation root on both sides of the facial reaction and uses branchless `يسطون` only as the textual action aimed at the reciters.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies connection, severance, scheme, rage, and a doubled recitation relay; I supply the arrow that the assault seeks to cut transmission by attacking its carriers. A live alternative is spontaneous rage with no strategic interruption function.

changed_reading.before: The hearers nearly lash out because they are angry.
changed_reading.after: Their near-assault is also a failed censorship mechanism: sever the carrier when the continuing sign-sequence cannot be severed by argument.

context_deltas.mechanism: Divine mention in 22:35 travels inward as heart-fear and restrained endurance. Recitation in the focus travels outward as facial distortion and nearly unrestrained force. The two scenes therefore coexist as opposite bodily processing routes for received divine speech.

activation_trace.role: Divine mention running on the tongue supplies the auditory input parallel to recitation.
Fear inwardly felt by the heart supplies the receptive body's first response.
The heart supplies the inward processing site contrasted with the focus face.
Self-restraint from panic supplies the containment absent from the almost-assault.
Following voices supply the corresponding spoken input in the focus scene.
Readable facial marks supply the rejecting body's outward response channel.

structural_cues: Both scenes begin with divine language reaching hearers and then name a bodily locus.
22:35 moves from heart-fear to restraint; 22:72 moves from face-mark to almost-assault.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two bodily responses to divine language; I infer that their opposite directions form a reception polarity. A live alternative is that the heart and face scenes are separate audience portraits with no designed physiological contrast.

changed_reading.before: The focus describes an isolated angry crowd.
changed_reading.after: The crowd exemplifies one of two somatic pathways: received speech can descend into a restrained, trembling heart or erupt through the face toward another body.

context_deltas.mechanism: The defense sequence of 22:38-40 protects attacked people and prevents the demolition of places where God's name is voiced. This scales the focus assault from a private flare-up to pressure against a public remembrance network; attacking reciters is one local way to attack the continued audibility of signs.

activation_trace.role: Warding away harm supplies protective counter-pressure around threatened believers.
Combat between parties supplies the social scale behind an individual threatened assault.
Repelling harm through people supplies the mechanism that keeps voiced worship possible.
Pulling down a structure supplies the larger destructive outcome that defense prevents.
The divine name running on tongues identifies audibility as what protected places sustain.
Voice following voice makes the reciters portable nodes of the protected remembrance network.

structural_cues: 22:38-40 moves from divine defense to attacked people, threatened buildings, and abundant voiced remembrance.
22:72 directs the threatened force specifically at those carrying the recitation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies protection of people and remembrance sites; I infer that violence against reciters is a portable form of the same suppression pressure. A live alternative is that the defense passage concerns communal expulsion and buildings, not the focus encounter.

changed_reading.before: The focus is an interpersonal confrontation between readers and angry hearers.
changed_reading.after: The confrontation is a micro-instance of pressure on the infrastructure of remembrance: silence the mobile voice when the sign and its public circulation cannot be contained.

context_deltas.mechanism: The travel question in 22:46 builds a perceptual circuit of ears, reasoning hearts, eyes, and blindness, then locates failure inside the chest rather than in functioning eyes. The focus face becomes the external output of that failed circuit: clear signs are heard, but inner cognition refuses uptake and the blockage emerges visibly and bodily.

activation_trace.role: The heart supplies the inner organ whose state governs the outward response.
Reason as a restraint on ignorance supplies the uptake function that fails.
Hearing as understanding and compliance supplies more than acoustic contact with recitation.
Blindness of heart and insight identifies the concealed failure behind a seeing face.
Working eyesight rules out simple sensory incapacity as the cause of refusal.
The source from which acts issue locates the causal blockage inside the chest.
Recognition from an effect lets the visible face be read back toward its hidden cause.

structural_cues: 22:46 explicitly contrasts unblinded eyes with blinded hearts inside chests.
22:72 begins with heard recitation, identifies a facial effect, and then approaches bodily action.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the hearing-heart-sight circuit and relocates blindness inward; I infer that the face in the focus externalizes this failed uptake. A live alternative is that the face reports social hostility without diagnosing a cognitive circuit.

changed_reading.before: The hearers perceive the signs and then become angry.
changed_reading.after: Acoustic and visual faculties remain intact, but inward understanding is blocked; the face and near-assault are outputs of heart-blindness rather than evidence that the signs were unclear.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context distinguishes impatient demand from a promise that does not fail, then pairs extended respite with eventual seizure and destination. This sharpens the focus's temporal asymmetry: their violence is almost immediate, while the answering fire may be delayed but is more certain than their incomplete act.

activation_trace.role: Haste supplies the human demand for immediate realization.
A promise failing at its appointment supplies the explicitly negated possibility.
Committed promise supplies certainty across a timescale larger than human impatience.
Extended time and respite supply the interval between wrongdoing and consequence.
Taking to account for an offense supplies the delayed transition into consequence.
Inevitable arrival at an end supplies the fixed terminus beyond respite.
Near-action supplies the attackers' compressed but still incomplete present time.
Threatening promise supplies the countertime whose delay does not weaken its force.

structural_cues: 22:47 denies failure of the promise while expanding a divine day beyond ordinary human scale.
22:48 orders respite, seizure, and destination; 22:72 orders near-assault, promise, and destination.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies haste, nonfailure, respite, seizure, and destination; I infer that 22:72 contrasts incomplete human immediacy with delayed divine certainty. A live alternative is that `almost` describes intensity only and carries no designed temporal contrast with the promise.

changed_reading.before: The attackers pose the immediate danger and fire is a remote add-on.
changed_reading.after: The apparent temporal advantage reverses: their immediate act remains incomplete, while the delayed counter-event is fixed by promise and destination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context first names striving against the signs in an effort to disable, then depicts a recitation exposed to hostile insertion, removal, and renewed stabilization. This activates the focus assault as the bodily layer of a wider interference ecology: if content cannot be disabled or corrupted, force turns toward the human relay.

activation_trace.role: Incapacity and making action fail supply the stated aim of striving against the signs.
Messenger and message supply the authorized transmission channel exposed to interference.
Recitation read and placed in sequence supplies the direct transmission analogue to the focus's doubled reciting.
Casting an item into a field supplies the intrusive move against transmission.
Removal followed by replacement supplies repair of the attempted insertion.
Tight stabilization and exactness supply the secured state of the signs after interference.
Continuous succession anchors the repaired transmission model in the focus's two recitation clauses.

structural_cues: 22:51 joins hostile striving directly to the signs; 22:52 orders transmission, insertion, removal, and stabilization.
22:72 repeats recitation before naming force aimed specifically at those who perform it.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies semantic interference and repair at prophetic transmission plus striving to disable signs; I infer that the focus assault is a physical version aimed at downstream carriers. A live alternative is that prophetic interference and audience violence operate at distinct levels without a shared mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The crowd attacks individual reciters in a self-contained scene.
changed_reading.after: The reciters occupy a resilient transmission system: hostile insertion is repaired, hostile disabling fails, and bodily force becomes the next attempted point of interruption.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately following parable commands listening, displays a tiny taker, and ends with seeker and sought unable to retrieve what was taken. Read back into the focus, the almost-assault is not proof of mastery but compensatory reach: force appears where listening, answering, and recovery fail.

activation_trace.role: Rendering a comparison visible supplies the interpretive lens placed directly after the focus.
Listening as understanding and compliance supplies the response that near-assault displaces.
The tiny fly supplies the deliberately disproportionate agent that exposes pretended power.
Extraction from another's possession supplies the recovery action they cannot perform.
The opposite of strength supplies the explicit verdict on the grasping parties.
Seeking and searching supply the futile reach shared by seeker and sought.
Seeking with difficulty supplies a focus-side echo of frustrated effort near the assault wording.

structural_cues: 22:73 immediately follows the near-assault with `listen`, failed retrieval, and the weakness of seeker and sought.
The focus's branchless `يسطون` remains a textual image of forceful reach but receives no invented branch citation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, a command to listen, failed retrieval, and explicit weakness; I infer that the prior violent reach compensates for inability to master the sign. A live alternative is that 22:73 targets the impotence of invoked beings only and does not reread the attackers.

changed_reading.before: The hearers nearly overpower the vulnerable reciters.
changed_reading.after: Their violent reach is itself evidence of weakness: unable to listen, answer, or recover control, they display force at the carrier of what exceeds them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence selects messengers, commissions messenger and community as witnesses, demands exertion, and commands protective attachment. This turns the focus reciters from anonymous speakers into downstream nodes of a selected witness relay; violence against them targets testimony, while attachment preserves collective continuity.

activation_trace.role: Choosing a purified selection supplies authorization at the head of the relay.
Messenger and message supply the first commissioned carriers.
Exertion under difficulty supplies the relay's persistence under resistance.
Testimony stated from knowledge supplies the social office carried through messenger and community.
A preserving hold supplies collective continuity when individual carriers face pressure.
One element following another anchors the focus reciters as links rather than isolated performers.

structural_cues: 22:75 moves from divine selection to messengers; 22:78 extends witness status from messenger to community.
The focus repeats recitation and identifies the threatened people by their relay function, `those who recite`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies selection, messengerhood, witness succession, exertion, and preserving attachment; I infer that the focus reciters belong functionally to this relay. A live alternative is that they are immediate readers only and should not be assigned a formal witness office.

changed_reading.before: The targets are incidental individuals reading aloud.
changed_reading.after: They are functional links in a selected witness chain, so assault on their bodies is pressure against transmitted testimony rather than merely against private speakers.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the form-distant split mapping from `ت ل و` to `ت ل ل`, not the normal sense of recitation. It remains anchored in the focus's repeated recitation, face, almost-assault, and destination, while 22:31 supplies an explicit fall-and-cast trajectory. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory lexical-spatial echo, never as a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The same focus scene repeats recitation, names faces, approaches bodily force, and closes on a destination.

activation_trace.role: Casting someone down onto brow or face supplies the distant overthrow echo inside the repeated recitation root.
A struck face supplies the bodily surface that makes the overthrow echo locally visible.
Noisy, unstable falling supplies the start of the context's bodily trajectory.
Falling into an abyss supplies continued forced motion away from stable standing.
Extreme distance supplies the remote terminus of the fall trajectory.
Final arrival anchors the exploratory fall image back in the focus's explicit destination.

changed_reading.before: Recitation is followed by a threat of assault and then a bad destination.
changed_reading.after: An exploratory overthrow echo makes the scene a contest over bodily direction: hearers threaten to cast down carriers, while the ayah redirects attention to the attackers' own final trajectory.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the split `ش ر ي` inventory beneath focus `ش ر ر`, so exchange is form-distant from the ordinary comparative `worse`. It remains anchored in the explicit comparison, committed promise, evaluative blame, and destination. Downstream prose should qualify it as a transactional analogy for moral countervalue, not translate `شر` as buying or selling.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The question `shall I tell you of worse than that` evaluates the near-assault against promised fire and a blamed destination.

activation_trace.role: Exchange between sale and purchase supplies an exploratory countervalue structure for `worse than that`.
Comparison with a counterpart supplies the explicit weighing relation between threatened violence and fire.
Committed obligation supplies the liability that makes the countervalue more than a passing comparison.
Formal blame supplies the negative valuation assigned to the settlement.
Arrival at the outcome supplies the point at which the exploratory countervalue is realized.

changed_reading.before: Fire is simply said to be worse than the violence they contemplate.
changed_reading.after: The comparison can also be carried as a contained countervalue model: attempted coercion incurs a promised, negatively valued settlement at the final destination.

strongest_changes: The face changed from a transparent anger display into an involuntary counter-sign, a directional turn, and the outer output of failed inward hearing.
The almost-assault changed from spontaneous rage into coexisting interruption, suppression, and compensatory-weakness models aimed at a resilient recitation relay.
The promised fire changed from a remote add-on into delayed but fixed countertime and a final disclosure of what denial presently leaks through the face.
summary.what_was_special: The double recitation around the facial clause, the adjacent command to listen, the transmission-interference sequence in 22:51-52, and the split mappings `ت ل و` to `ت ل ل`, `ك و د` to `ك ي د`, and `ش ر ر` to `ش ر ي` kept spatial, causal, temporal, social, and exchange readings alive without forcing a single resolution.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus root `س ط و` has no branch inventory, so its assault image supports structural cues only and receives no invented branch citation.
The split-root overthrow, machination, and exchange activations are form-distant and should remain exploratory rather than lexical replacements.
The context parallels may be rhetorical echoes rather than direct causal explanations of the focus crowd.
